one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event dominates the window: Q3 2026 results after the close on Tue 2026-10-20. Consensus is about $2.64 non-GAAP EPS on about $2.91B revenue. The comparison is tough: Q3 2025 da Vinci procedures grew ~19%, and its $2.40 EPS included a $0.12 tax benefit. H1 2026 da Vinci procedure growth was ~15.5% (16% Q1, 15% Q2), and the guide is 13.5-15.5% 'closer to the midpoint', which implies only ~13-14% in H2. Management also promised to quantify the 2027 Extended Use Program on this call. On the Q2 call BofA floated a ~5-point I&A-per-procedure impact spread over a couple of years (the 2020 program was modeled at ~7%). Management calls it 'directionally similar to 2020', with a 'gradual' net decline, so the sizing is more likely to land as a headwind than a relief. Against that, the 2020 precedent ended near -2%, and the Wells Fargo commentary (Sept 9) kept the outlook. Since round 1 of my work: the stock rallied from $350 (Sept 8) to $415 (Sept 28) on that commentary and the Sept 22 EU approvals, and closed $401 today. That removes the cushion the July low had given, and HCA's Q2 elective-surgery weakness argues against a US re-acceleration print. ISRG has beaten EPS consensus four quarters running, but the stock has fallen on two of the last prints despite beats. Net: a slight negative skew. I put the median at ~$398 with a monthly sigma of ~11.5% (37%/3.5 plus an earnings-gap premium), so P(>= spot) is 0.48. That is a small tilt, not a confident call. Round-2 check: the supervisor's fact-checks confirmed the Oct 20 date, the ~19% Q3 2025 procedure comp and that the EUP has not yet been sized (Trefis 2026-09-18). The Sept 16 Fed hike with the 10-year at 5.01% is a mild multiple headwind but already in the price. Nothing in the follow-up changed the 1-month view, so the ladder is unchanged (median ~$398-399, sigma ~11.5%, P(>=spot)=0.48).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%: 2028E non-GAAP EPS $13.4 x 31x = $415; EUP range 1-3% gives $408-423) and a 10-year FCF DCF (40%: 2027 FCF $3.5B, 12.5%/8.5% growth, WACC raised to 8.75% with the 10-year at 5.01%, 4% terminal, $8.63B cash, 355M diluted shares, rolled forward 12 months = ~$380). Blend ~$401, about spot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E non-GAAP EPS $13.4 x 31x forward P/E (NTM basis as of Oct-2027). EUP sensitivity: 1% drag -> 2028E ~$13.65 ($423); 3% drag -> ~$13.15 ($408).

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 actual $2.50 + $2.80 = $5.30 (Q2 included a ~$36M IEEPA tariff refund). H2 consensus is ~$5.48 (Q3 ~$2.64), for FY consensus $10.78. I add ~$0.12 for ISRG's record of four straight beats.

Consensus is $12.09-12.33 (low $11.05) [24]. The EUP has not been sized [33][9]. I now carry a 1-3% 2027 I&A/procedure drag centred on ~2% rather than 2-3%. My own primary check of the 2020 program [32][8]: I&A/procedure was ~$1,960 in 2019 ($2.41B / ~1.23M procedures), ~$1,980 in 2020 (Q4 2020 stocking orders inflate it) and ~$1,945 in 2021 ($3.10B / 1.594M). That is a net ~-1% over two years despite an advanced-instrument mix tailwind, so the gross effect was perhaps 4-6% spread over 2-3 years. That fits a ~2% net drag in year one better than BofA's ~5-point framing, though COVID distorts it. On ~$8.0B of 2027 I&A (Q2 2026 run rate $1.73B/qtr [1] grown ~13%), each point of drag is ~$80M of revenue, ~$0.17-0.18 EPS. At the 2% midpoint 2027E is ~$12.0, ~1% below consensus.

2027E $12.0 grown ~12%: ~12% procedure growth, the residual EUP drag in 2028, limited op-margin leverage (non-GAAP op margin ~41-42%) and ~1% net share shrink (diluted 364.1M -> 357.3M over the year to Q2 2026 [1]; $4.7B authorization left [2]). Below aggregator 2028 consensus of $13.91 [24].

Today's $401 is ~33x 2027 consensus ($12.2). I keep 31x for Oct-2027: EPS growth decelerates toward low teens; the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 with more hikes signalled and the 10-year closed at 5.01% [31][34], which argues against holding 33x; Ottava (De Novo 2026-07-22) and Hugo enter US soft tissue [21][19]; and the Ninth Circuit SIS reversal [15] raises aftermarket antitrust risk. The ~1-turn discount (~$13/share) already covers the supervisor's ~$5/share litigation EV haircut, so I do not deduct it again.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: 2027 FCF $3.5B (~26% margin on ~$13.3B revenue); growth 12.5% yrs 2-5, 8.5% yrs 6-10; terminal growth 4%; WACC 8.75%; cash $8.63B, no debt; 355M diluted shares; PV today ~$349/share, rolled forward one year ~$380

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 2026 OCF $1,972.9M less capex $215.9M = $1.76B (31% margin), but OCF includes a $370.3M deferred-tax swing. Management called 31% 'about as high as we've done in history' vs a 22% long-term average. Normalizing for the tax item gives ~25%. 2026 revenue ~$11.8B (consensus $11.76B) grown ~13% = ~$13.3B x ~26% = ~$3.5B.

da Vinci procedures went from +18% (2025) to a 13.5-15.5% guide (2026), H1 ~15.5%, implied H2 ~13-14%. Installed base +12%, Ion +36%, OUS +20%, US +12%. Low-teens for four years, fading as the base grows and EUP pricing bites.

Debt-free large-cap medtech. With the 10-year at 5.01% after the 2026-09-16 hike [31][34], my round-1 8.5% left only ~3.5 points over the risk-free rate for a stock with 37% realized vol and new litigation and competitive risk; I raise it to 8.75%. Sensitivity: 8.5% -> ~$400, 9.0% -> ~$362. 4% terminal for a franchise with a long procedure runway.
Cash $2,760.4M + short-term $2,455.8M + long-term investments $3,409.3M at 2026-06-30; no debt.

Q2 2026 diluted weighted average 357.3M (basic 354.1M) per the Q2 release [1]; 353.3M basic outstanding at 2026-07-16 per the 10-Q cover [2]. Buybacks shrink the diluted count ~1-2%/yr but dilution offsets part of it, so ~355M is the right per-share base. Round 1 wrongly used the basic count less buybacks (351M).

bear.story: US da Vinci growth slides to high single digits. ACA attrition (HCA Q2 10-Q: same-facility uninsured admissions +23.4%, exchange admissions -15%, outpatient surgeries -3.4%) is compounded by Medicaid work requirements from 2027-01-01. The EUP lands at the top of the 1-3% range or above, with little elasticity. SIS proceeds on remand and the hospital class trial (2027-09-14) goes badly, opening the instrument aftermarket. Ottava and Hugo lengthen selling cycles. Rates stay above 5%. 2028E EPS ~$12.0 at ~24.5x.

base.story: Procedures grow ~12-13% in 2027. The EUP trims I&A/procedure ~2% in 2027 (range 1-3%), partly offset by da Vinci 5 mix, SP, Ion and buybacks. EPS ~$12.0 (2027) and ~$13.4 (2028E), multiple ~31x NTM with the 10-year near 5%. Litigation stays unresolved and is not material within the horizon.

bull.story: Deferred procedures return (HCA expects 2027 coverage loss to be smaller than 2026). The EUP lands near 1% net, as the 2019-21 filings suggest the 2020 program did, and drives elasticity in benign and ASC procedures. Cardiac, SP and the da Vinci 5 upgrade cycle keep growth near 15%. En banc rehearing helps in SIS. The multiple re-rates to ~36.5x on ~$14.2 2028E; I no longer use 38x with the 10-year above 5%.

thesis_break_reason: $300 is ~9% below the July 2026 low ($328.57) and ~25x 2027 consensus ($12.09), below my 31x base even on a reduced EPS path. A trade there would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than 37%-vol noise. Candidates: an EUP sizing on Oct 20 well beyond ~3% of I&A/procedure or front-loaded into 2027, a 2027 procedure guide below ~11%, an adverse SIS/class-action development (the Ninth Circuit revived SIS on 2026-08-13; the class trial starts 2027-09-14) that forces open the EndoWrist aftermarket, or evidence that Ottava/Hugo are winning US general-surgery placements.

Ninth Circuit decision on Intuitive's en banc rehearing petition in SIS (filed ~2026-09-28)
US midterms; Polymarket prices near-zero odds of enhanced ACA credits being extended (vol ~$407K)
FOMC meeting; the Sept 16 dot plot signalled another hike in 2026, and a move keeps the 10-year near or above 5%
Preliminary FY2026 results and 2027 procedure guide (mid-January); Medicaid work requirements apply by 2027-01-01

Extended Use Program launch on benign-procedure EndoWrist instruments; Ottava limited US launch expands; possible Hugo general-surgery 510(k) clearance (filed 2026-06-03; no timeline given, so a headline risk at any time)
Q1 2027 earnings; first quarter of EUP revenue impact
China centralized tenders / new charge codes (management expects clarity in 2027); ~250 systems left in quota
EndoWrist repair/replacement antitrust class action trial (class certified 2025-03-31)
Tariffs: Section 122 10% expired 2026-07-24, replaced by Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5%; USMCA exclusion matters for Mexico-made instruments; IEEPA refunds subject to appeal

key_uncertainties: EUP sizing (quantified 2026-10-20): the 2020 program was modeled at $150-170M (~6.6% of 2019 I&A). My own read of the 2019-21 10-K figures is a net ~-1% I&A/procedure over two years, distorted by COVID and stocking orders. BofA's ~5-point framing is the other end. I carry a 1-3% 2027 drag (EPS ~$11.8-12.15).

US procedure trajectory: HCA's Q2 10-Q shows same-facility uninsured admissions +23.4%, exchange admissions -15% and outpatient surgeries -3.4%, against ISRG US +12%. Medicaid work requirements in 2027 (CBO: 4.8M lose coverage) vs HCA's view that 2027 coverage loss is smaller than 2026.

Antitrust: Ninth Circuit reversed the SIS judgment (2026-08-13), finding evidence of >99% foremarket share. En banc petition pending, hospital class trial on 2027-09-14. Treble damages and possible remedies that open the instrument aftermarket.
Competition: J&J Ottava De Novo (2026-07-22) covers core general surgery incl. hernia, chole and bariatrics. Medtronic Hugo filed for general/gyn. Management says selling cycles are unchanged so far.
Multiple: ~33x 2027 consensus today. The Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 and the 10-year is at ~5%, and growth is slowing. Whether the multiple compresses further dominates the range.
FCF quality: the H1 31% FCF margin was helped by a $370M deferred-tax swing; normalized ~25%.
reasoning: Round 2, same primary-document lane. The supervisor graded my sources high and found no lane drift. Its feedback, and how I acted on it: (1) EUP: I had used only the BofA ~5-point framework. I checked the 2020 analog against primary filings myself (FY2021 10-K). I&A/procedure went from ~$1,960 (2019) to ~$1,945 (2021), a net ~-1% over two years with an advanced-instrument mix tailwind, and Q4 2020 stocking distorts 2020. That supports the supervisor's view that the lower end is plausible, but COVID makes it a weak base rate. I now carry a 1-3% 2027 drag centred on 2%, not 2-3%. 2027E rises to $12.0 (from $11.9) and 2028E to $13.4 (from $13.3). (2) Shares: corrected 351M to ~355M diluted (Q2 diluted weighted average 357.3M, verified in the release). (3) Rates: I verified the 2026-09-16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% and the 10-year at 5.01%. I keep 31x on P/E (the supervisor agrees). I also raise the DCF WACC from 8.5% to 8.75%, since 8.5% left too thin a premium over a 5% risk-free rate. This is where I go further than the supervisor: DCF $404 -> ~$380. (4) Litigation: I agree the SIS reversal plus the 2027-09-14 class trial is a left-tail item. My 1-turn multiple discount already exceeds the ~$5/share EV haircut, so I do not deduct twice. (5) HCA: my figures were confirmed; I add uninsured admissions +23.4%. Valuation: P/E $415 (60%) and DCF $380 (40%) blend to ~$401, at spot and below the supervisor's ~$420. The gap is mainly my higher WACC and the 2028E EPS ($13.4 vs $13.5). Scenarios at 25/50/25 give $295/$415/$520 (mean ~$411); the bull case is trimmed from 38x to 36.5x for rates. Ladder: lognormal, median ~$404, sigma ~0.34 (near 37% realized vol), a slightly fatter left tail for the class trial inside the horizon. P(>=401) = 0.508, from 0.525. 1-month ladder unchanged (P(>=spot) 0.48): the Oct 20 print against a +19% comp after a September rally. Research: 4 searches/fetches plus 2 SEC filings, so research was limited by design. No option data was consulted, and nothing under valuation/priors/ or round1_capped/ was opened.
